newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-Rixon retains same team despite loss.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Rixon retains same team despite loss.

text.p: SHARJAH, Nov 10 - Sunday's four-wicket loss to Pakistan has not dented the confidence of the New Zealand cricket team, NZPA reports.
Coach Steve Rixon underlined that when he named an unchanged team for Monday's (tonight NZT) encounter with World Cup champions Sri Lanka.
No serious consideration was given to making changes to the top order batting personnel despite their second failure on Sunday in as many matches during the Champions Trophy one-day series here.

Nathan Astle and Craig Spearman both made zero on Sunday while Stephen Fleming doubled his series run haul to two as Pakistan's famed new ball pair Waqar Younis and captain Wasim Akram humbled the top order.
Captain Lee Germon's faith in his frontline batsmen has not been shaken by their struggle to find their early-season feet.
"I am not worried about the top order. I have faith in the talent that is there," he said.
"We've had a couple of rough starts but these guys have been picked because of the ability they have. I have complete faith they're going to come through.
"When you are playing Waqar and Wasim you run the risk of being two or three down quickly because they are such lethal bowlers.
"They can produce the unplayable and I think Nathan got one of those today."
Astle, who scored three one-day centuries for New Zealand last summer, has started his new campaign with consecutive ducks.
He received a magnificent first-up delivery from Younis today, which was extremely fast, swung late and careered into the stumps.
"It wasn't exactly the sort of ball you want to get first up, but I should have played a lot straighter than I did," Astle said.
"Obviously I've now missed twice, and I want to get the team off to a good start with 'Spearsie'.
"I'm sure I'll come right. I'm sure it's not a major problem. I'm still confident and I'm seeing the ball well."
New Zealand beat Sri Lanka by 29 runs in the series opener last Thursday and Rixon said it was important his players dwelt on that instead of Sunday's defeat.
"They can reflect on what happened today and learn from it, but they should dwell on the sweet taste of success from the previous match," he added.
Wellington medium pacer Gavin Larsen, who is still recovering from a calf muscle strain, is getting closer to full fitness but wasn't considered for the Sri Lankan match.

Sri Lanka have their own worries. Offspinner Kumara Dharmasena has been ruled out of the match because of a shoulder injury sustained while fielding during his team's victory over Pakistan last Friday.
Teams:
New Zealand: Lee Germon (captain), Nathan Astle, Craig Spearman, Adam Parore, Stephen Fleming, Chris Cairns, Mark Greatbatch, Chris Harris, Dipak Patel, Simon Doull, Danny Morrison.

Sri Lanka (from): Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Aravinda de Silva, Sanath Jayasuriya, Roshan Mahanama, Asanka Gurusinha, Hashan Tillekaratne, Muttiah Muralitharan, Ravindra Pushpakumara, Chaminda Vaas, Romesh Kaluwitharana, Upul Chandana, Sanjeewa Silva.
